To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) IP LPS administration in rats results in an inflammatory cytokine response, 2) the cytokine response to IP LPS administration is more variable than the response to IV administration, 3) the IP cytokine response to LPS can be characterized by curve fitting, and 4) electrical vagus stimulation can be used to selectively modulate cytokines.

the IP LPS challenge in rats produces a consistent order of cytokine response, that this order is distinct from the order of response to IV LPS challenges in rats, that the IP LSP challenge is variable in starting time, that the subdiaphragmatic vagal nerve can be selectively stimulated to produce effects on the IP LPS cytokines, and that the effects of the stimulation on IP LPS cytokinesis are variable and distinct for each subdiaphragmatic nerve branch stimulated.

we found there to exist a consistent order of the IP LPS cytokines response, that the response to IP LPS was more variable than in IV LPS challenges and occurred later, that there are specific effects on multiple cytokines by each of the subdiaphragmatic nerve stimulation subsets, and that IP LPS is an acceptable, arguably more physiolgically relevant, method for use in rat models when our methods are utilized.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the characterization of the IP LPS inflammatory cascade in rats and the modulation of this cascade by subdiaphragmatic vagus nerve stimulation.
the biological mechanisms of vagus nerve stimulation (Vagus Nerve Stimulation) and its role in inflammatory disease.
the characterization of IP LPS and the subsequent effects of subdiaphragmatic VNS in rats, and the implications that our findings have on inflammatory disease treatment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
subdiaphragmatic VNS can be utilized in a targeted manner to modulate inflammatory responses in the rat body.
IP LPS administration is a viable and practical method for inducing inflammation in rats when using the methods described in this study, but IV administration remains the gold standard.
subdiaphragmatic vagus nerve stimulation has a significant and selective effect on the inflammatory response of the body, and this effect is dependent on the vagal branch stimulated.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the vagus nerve has the capacity for selective modulation of inflammatory responses, which may have implications for the treatment of inflammatory disease.
subdiaphragmatic vagus nerve stimulation can be used to regulate the cytokine response to LPS challenge in a time-variant, selective manner.
subdiaphragmatic VNS has a significant role in the modulation of inflammatory responses and can be used as a treatment for inflammatory disorders.
The main takeaway from our work is that
subdiaphragmatic vagus nerve stimulation can be utilized to modulate inflammatory cytokine levels in a specific, time- and location-dependent manner.
IP LPS can be a useful tool to study inflammatory responses in rats, and that subdiaphragmatic vagal neurostimulation is a promising tool to modulate inflammatory response.
the IP LPS challenge is a useful tool for the study of vagal inflammatory modulation in rats.
